## Intent

**Problem:** Meus Registros' funnel button is a no-op (spec-5-1) — there is no way to narrow the plain timeline by entry source or date range, and `EntriesRepository.list()` has no filter parameters to call.

**Approach:** Extend `list()` with `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`; add a filter bottom sheet and a removable active-filter-chip row to `MeusRegistrosCubit`'s existing plain-timeline branch. Filters apply only to the unfiltered list path this story — combining them with an active search term is story 5.3.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- `EntriesRepository.list({String? cursor, int limit = 20, EntrySource? source, DateTime? dateFrom, DateTime? dateTo})`; `EntriesRemoteDataSource.list()` forwards non-null values as `source`(`.name`)/`dateFrom`/`dateTo` (ISO-8601) to `entries-list`, mirroring `search()`'s existing convention.
- Source is single-choice (`EntrySource?`, not a `Set`) — see Design Notes.
- `MeusRegistrosCubit` gains `applyFilters({source, dateFrom, dateTo})`/`clearFilters()` (own methods, not `loadFirstPage()` — see Design Notes); both bump `_generation`, replace state via `list()`. `_fetchMore()` carries active filters forward alongside `cursor`.
- `_offlineFallback()` stays as-is (full unfiltered box dump, same `cursor == null` trigger) — offline + filters silently returns the full cached list (AD-9: cache is never locally filtered).
- New `EntriesFilterSheet` + static `.show()`, mirroring `InsertionModal.show()`'s pattern (`isScrollControlled`, `useSafeArea`, `colorScrimHeavy`, Reduce-Motion-aware `durationSheetUp`). Groups: "INTERVALO DE DATA" (Todo o período/Esta semana/Este mês → computed `dateFrom`/`dateTo`) and "TIPO DE ENTRADA" (manual/áudio/foto/chat), both single-choice. No "CATEGORIA". "Aplicar" commits via `cubit.applyFilters(...)` + closes; "Limpar" resets only the sheet's pending selection.
- Active-filters chip row renders under the search bar, only inside the existing `ResourceIdle` branch (`meus_registros_screen.dart:209`), when any filter is active; each chip removable ("x", re-applies the rest); "Limpar filtros" link calls `cubit.clearFilters()`. Chips: `colorSecondary`/`colorCategoryChipText`/`radiusFull`.
- `EntriesSearchBar` gains `onFilterTap` (replaces `onPressed: () {}`, line 63) and `hasActiveFilters` (fills the funnel icon).

**Ask First:** none — scope pinned by `epic-5-context.md` and RF06.

**Never:** filter params on `EntriesSearchCubit`/`search()`, or a combined search+filter query (story 5.3); a "CATEGORIA"/tag group (extension, forbidden); client-side filtering/sorting of the cached box; a new cubit/DI registration.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Source filter only | Aplicar with "áudio" selected | query `source=audio`; results narrowed | N/A |
| Source + date range together | both selected, Aplicar | one query, both params — AND narrowing | N/A |
| Remove one of two active chips | tap "x" on the source chip | re-queries with only the date range | N/A |
| Clear all filters | "Limpar filtros" link tapped | full unfiltered list restored in place, no reload/re-mount | N/A |
| Load more with filters active | scroll to bottom, filters active | `_fetchMore` sends `cursor` + same filters | N/A |
| Offline, filters active, first page | no connectivity | `_offlineFallback()`'s full unfiltered cached dump renders, no error shown | N/A (cache content silently ignores filters, per AD-9) |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `entries_repository.dart:38` -- `list()` signature to extend
- `entries_remote_data_source.dart:54-61` -- query-param building to extend
- `entries_repository_impl.dart:55-95` (`list()`), `:189-208` (`_offlineFallback()`, stays filter-oblivious)
- `meus_registros_cubit.dart:58` (`_generation`), `:138-140` (`loadFirstPage()`), `:223-225` (`_fetchMore()`)
- `meus_registros_screen.dart:198` (search bar docking), `:201-237` (`ResourceIdle` fork — chip row + sheet mount here)
- `entries_search_bar.dart:19,58-72` -- funnel no-op to replace with `onFilterTap`/`hasActiveFilters`
- `insertion_modal.dart:63-135` -- bottom-sheet `.show()` pattern to mirror
- `entry.dart:6` -- `EntrySource` enum (manual/audio/photo/chat), confirmed no `tags` field to touch
- `design_tokens.dart` -- reuse `colorSecondary`/`colorCategoryChipText`/`radiusFull`/`radiusLg`/`elevation2`/`textMonoCaption`/`durationSheetUp`/`colorScrimHeavy`; no new token

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [x] `entries_repository.dart` -- add `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo` params to `list()`
- [x] `entries_remote_data_source.dart` -- forward new params as query params to `entries-list`
- [x] `entries_repository_impl.dart` -- pass params through; leave `_offlineFallback()` untouched
- [x] `meus_registros_cubit.dart` -- add `applyFilters()`/`clearFilters()`; carry filters into `_fetchMore()`
- [x] `presentation/widgets/entries_filter_sheet.dart` (new) -- date-range + source groups, Aplicar/Limpar
- [x] `entries_search_bar.dart` -- `onFilterTap` + `hasActiveFilters` (filled icon)
- [x] `meus_registros_screen.dart` -- wire sheet trigger; render active-filter chip row in the `ResourceIdle` branch
- [x] Unit tests covering every I/O Matrix row across the new/changed files
- [x] Widget tests: filter sheet (selection, Aplicar/Limpar), chip row (remove one, clear all), filled funnel icon

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given the filter sheet, when "áudio" + a date range are both applied, then the single `entries-list` query carries both params and results narrow with AND logic.
- Given active filters, when "Limpar filtros" is tapped, then the full unfiltered list renders in place without a screen reload or re-mount.
- Given active filters, when the user scrolls to load more, then the continuation request carries the same filters alongside `cursor`.
- Given the device is offline with filters active on the first page, when the fallback fires, then it shows the full cached list, not a filtered or empty one.

## Design Notes

TIPO DE ENTRADA is single-choice, not multi-choice as the prototype's chip row suggests: `source` (openapi.yaml, both endpoints) accepts exactly one enum value, and AD-9 forbids merging multiple per-source queries client-side — the prototype is a visual reference, not an API contract, so the frozen backend wins.

`applyFilters()`/`clearFilters()` are separate from `loadFirstPage()` because that method's doc contract is "always re-fetch on mount" — reusing it for an in-session filter change would conflate two different triggers.

- `fvm flutter analyze` -- expected: zero issues
- `fvm flutter test` -- expected: all tests pass

The contract (`docs/input/backend/api/openapi.yaml:510-521`) declares `dateFrom`/`dateTo` as `format: date-time` (RFC3339, which expects an explicit offset). If the backend parses the offset-less string as UTC, a user outside UTC+0 selecting "Esta semana"/"Este mês" gets a filter window shifted by their own UTC offset — entries from the first/last few hours of the intended range can be silently included or excluded.
  
  - **Confirmed/pending entries bypass the active filter.** `MeusRegistrosCubit._onEntryConfirmed`/`_onPendingWritesChanged` (`lib/features/entries/presentation/cubit/meus_registros_cubit.dart:85-153`) unconditionally prepend the new/pending `Entry` into `MeusRegistrosLoaded.entries`, with no check against `_activeSource`/`_activeDateFrom`/`_activeDateTo`. If a user has `source: audio` active and then saves a new manual-text entry via the Insertion Modal, that manual entry is prepended on top of the supposedly "audio-only" filtered list, visibly contradicting the active filter chip. No test combines `applyFilters()` with a pending/confirmed write.
  
  - **Active-filter chips stay visible and "on" during an offline cache fallback that silently ignores the filter.** `EntriesRepositoryImpl._offlineFallback()` (`lib/features/entries/data/repositories/entries_repository_impl.dart:200-219`) always returns the entire unfiltered Hive-box dump on `networkOffline`/`networkTimeout` (by design, AD-9), but `_ActiveFiltersRow` in `lib/features/entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen.dart` renders purely off `cubit.hasActiveFilters` with no distinction for "filter requested but not actually applied because the cache fallback fired." A user offline with a filter chip showing sees the full unfiltered timeline with nothing telling them the filter had no effect.
  
  - **The "active filter" funnel indicator is shown even while viewing unrelated search results.** In `lib/features/entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen.dart`, `EntriesSearchBar.hasActiveFilters` is driven solely by `widget.cubit.hasActiveFilters`, independent of whether the on-screen content is the filtered timeline or `EntriesSearchCubit`'s own results (whose `search()` method was never extended with `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`). A user mid-search who previously applied a filter sees a filled "active" funnel icon next to search results that were never filtered, implying the search itself is filtered.
  
  - **The filter funnel stays reachable/functional while a search is in progress**, letting `applyFilters()`/`clearFilters()` silently mutate `MeusRegistrosCubit`'s hidden timeline state underneath a currently-visible, unrelated search surface. Nothing disables or hides the funnel button while `EntriesSearchCubit`'s state isn't idle, and no test exercises this interaction.

A filter applied just before a week/month rolls over (e.g. Sunday night, or the last day of a month) no longer matches either preset once that boundary passes, so the sheet falls back to pre-selecting "Todo o período" even though a date filter is still actively applied to the list — misrepresenting the current state to the user.

Dynamic Type" UX note and justifying its `SingleChildScrollView` wrapper specifically as a guard against overflow at the largest accessibility text size. Unlike the already-tracked, pre-existing `EntriesSearchBar` gap, this is new code added by this very change, shipped with zero verification that the guard actually prevents a clip/overflow.
  
  - **No widget-level test removes the date-range chip specifically, or exercises two active chips rendered together.** `meus_registros_screen_test.dart`'s "Acceptance Criteria" test for the active-filter chip row only taps the source chip's "x"; the "remove one of two active chips" scenario (`_ActiveFiltersRow` in `meus_registros_screen.dart`) is only exercised at the cubit level (`meus_registros_cubit_test.dart`), never through an actual UI tap with both `_ActiveFilterChip`s visible side by side.
  
  - **`EntriesFilterSheet.show()`'s reduce-motion branch has no test coverage.** It copies `InsertionModal.show()`'s reduce-motion-aware entrance/exit animation handling (`disableAnimations` → `Duration.zero`), but `InsertionModal` has a dedicated reduce-motion test (`test/features/capture/presentation/widgets/insertion_modal_test.dart`) while no test anywhere sets `MediaQuery.disableAnimations`/`AccessibilityFeatures` before opening the filter sheet (`entries_filter_sheet_test.dart` bypasses `.show()` entirely by pumping the widget directly; `meus_registros_screen_test.dart`'s filter tests never configure reduced motion either).
  
  - **Date-range boundary inclusivity is never exercised end-to-end.** `DateRangePreset.rangeFrom`'s doc comment in `entries_filter_sheet.dart` notes the spec is silent on inclusive/exclusive bounds and that this was decided unilaterally (AGENTS.md "decide and proceed" policy), but no repository/data-source/cubit test asserts what actually happens for an entry occurring exactly at `dateFrom` or `dateTo` — the chosen convention is documented but not verified against any fake/real response.

7	A brief secondary deletion check runs as Step 4 when the diff removes code.

17

Examples: missing else/default, unguarded inputs, off-by-one loops, arithmetic overflow, implicit type coercion, race conditions, timeout gaps
32	- Consider implicit branches: the diff special-cases or changes the handling of one or more members of a fixed set of values — enums, status codes, sentinels, type tags, flags, value ranges. The rest of the set is implicit branches (e.g. the diff changes the `RED` and `YELLOW` cases of a `RED`/`YELLOW`/`GREEN` enum; `GREEN` is the implicit branch)

# Edge Case Hunter Review

**Goal:** You are a pure path tracer. Never comment on whether code is good or bad; only list missing handling.
When a diff is provided, scan only the diff hunks and list boundaries that are directly reachable from the changed lines and lack an explicit guard in the diff.
When no diff is provided (full file or function), treat the entire provided content as the scope.
Ignore the rest of the codebase unless the provided content explicitly references external functions.
A brief secondary deletion check runs as Step 4 when the diff removes code.

**Inputs:**
- **content** — Content to review: diff, full file, or function
- **also_consider** (optional) — Areas to keep in mind during review alongside normal edge-case analysis

**MANDATORY: Execute steps in the Execution section IN EXACT ORDER. DO NOT skip steps or change the sequence. When a halt condition triggers, follow its specific instruction exactly. Each action within a step is a REQUIRED action to complete that step.**

**Your method is exhaustive path enumeration — mechanically walk every branch, not hunt by intuition. Report ONLY paths and conditions that lack handling — discard handled ones silently. Do NOT editorialize or add filler. Do not assign severity labels, rankings, or priority levels.**


## EXECUTION

### Step 1: Receive Content

- Load the content to review strictly from the parent message that launched you (not from this instruction file)
- If content is empty, or cannot be decoded as text, return `[{"location":"N/A","trigger_condition":"Input empty or undecodable","guard_snippet":"Provide valid content to review","potential_consequence":"Review skipped — no analysis performed"}]` and stop
- Identify content type (diff, full file, or function) to determine scope rules

### Step 2: Exhaustive Path Analysis

**Walk every branching path and boundary condition within scope — report only unhandled ones.**

- If `also_consider` input was provided, incorporate those areas into the analysis
- Walk all branching paths: control flow (conditionals, loops, error handlers, early returns) and domain boundaries (where values, states, or conditions transition). Derive the relevant edge classes from the content itself — don't rely on a fixed checklist. Examples: missing else/default, unguarded inputs, off-by-one loops, arithmetic overflow, implicit type coercion, race conditions, timeout gaps
- Consider implicit branches: the diff special-cases or changes the handling of one or more members of a fixed set of values — enums, status codes, sentinels, type tags, flags, value ranges. The rest of the set is implicit branches (e.g. the diff changes the `RED` and `YELLOW` cases of a `RED`/`YELLOW`/`GREEN` enum; `GREEN` is the implicit branch)
- For each path: determine whether the content handles it
- Collect only the unhandled paths as findings — discard handled ones silently

### Step 3: Validate Completeness

- Revisit every edge class from Step 2 — e.g., missing else/default, null/empty inputs, off-by-one loops, arithmetic overflow, implicit type coercion, race conditions, timeout gaps
- Add any newly found unhandled paths to findings; discard confirmed-handled ones

### Step 4: Deletion Check

If the diff removed or replaced meaningful code (ignore pure renames and whitespace): load `references/deletion-check.md` and follow it.

### Step 5: Present Findings

Output all findings as a single JSON array following the Output Format specification exactly.


## OUTPUT FORMAT

Return ONLY a valid JSON array of objects. Each edge-case finding contains exactly these four fields:

```json
[{
  "location": "file:start-end (or file:line when single line, or file:hunk when exact line unavailable)",
  "trigger_condition": "one-line description (max 15 words)",
  "guard_snippet": "minimal code sketch that closes the gap (single-line escaped string, no raw newlines or unescaped quotes)",
  "potential_consequence": "what could actually go wrong (max 15 words)"
}]
```

No extra text, no explanations, no markdown wrapping. An empty array `[]` is valid when nothing is found. Deletion findings from Step 4, if any, go in the same array with the extra fields defined in `references/deletion-check.md`.


## HALT CONDITIONS

- If content is empty or cannot be decoded as text, return `[{"location":"N/A","trigger_condition":"Input empty or undecodable","guard_snippet":"Provide valid content to review","potential_consequence":"Review skipped — no analysis performed"}]` and stop
<reference path="references/deletion-check.md">
# Deletion Check

Secondary pass for the Edge Case Hunter — runs only when the diff removed meaningful code. Subordinate to the edge-case pass; findings are usually few or none.

For each chunk of removed or replaced code (ignore pure renames and whitespace), ask: did it carry behavior or a contract that the change neither re-established nor intentionally retired? Add a finding for any resulting regression, orphaned reference, or newly-dead code. Skip anything already covered by your edge-case findings.

Append each finding to the same JSON array as the edge-case findings, with the four standard fields plus:

- `kind`: `"deletion"`
- `confidence`: `"high"`, `"medium"`, or `"low"` — these are inferences; rate them

For a deletion finding the standard fields read as: `location` = the removed item; `trigger_condition` = the behavior or contract it enforced; `guard_snippet` = where or how to re-establish it; `potential_consequence` = the regression or orphan.

Add nothing if nothing qualifies.
</reference>

## CONTENT SOURCE

Review the content supplied under "Review content:" in the message that launched you.

1	# Verification Gap Review
2	
3	**Goal:** Find changed behavior that could break without reliable verification catching it. Ask one question — "if the behavior this change is supposed to produce broke where it's actually used, would verification fail?" Do not hunt for correctness bugs, but report genuine problems you notice while tracing verification.
4	
5	The main verification gap shapes are:
6	
7	1. **Regression gap:** the changed code regresses where it's used, and no test covering that use would fail.
8	2. **Missing-adoption gap:** a place that should now use the new behavior doesn't; it handles the same case its own way, or not at all, and no test would flag the omission.
9	3. **Broken-verification gap:** a test appears to cover the changed behavior, but would not actually protect it because it is skipped, flaky, not run in the normal verification path, or too weak to observe the regression.
10	
11	## Evidence Rules
12	
13	- Read a test before claiming what it covers, runs, asserts, or misses.
14	- Before claiming no test exists, search the whole repo by the symbol under test and by import references; expected file locations are not enough.
15	- Never assert what you did not verify. If a finding cannot be grounded, drop it.
16	- In a finding, say what you actually checked — "none of the tests I read cover this" — and show how far you looked. Say a test doesn't exist anywhere only when the symbol/import-reference search actually shows that.
17	- Do not assign severity, confidence, priority, or ranking.
18	
19	## Review Sequence
20	
21	### Step 1: Screen for behavioral change
22	
23	Screen each part of the change separately. If a part is non-behavioral, skip it. Call a part non-behavioral only when the changed code does not alter return values, thrown errors, caller-visible side effects, or observable state (including iteration order and emitted messages). Once a part meets that test, move on; do not inspect callers or tests for extra confirmation.
24	
25	Common non-behavioral examples: formatting, comments, whitespace; pure renames; trivial getters/setters and pass-throughs; type-only or compiler-enforced changes with no runtime effect; etc.
26	
27	Only outcomes produced by deterministic code are worth automatically testing; tests are useless on static source text and brittle on LLM output. Skip those parts.
28	
29	If every part is skipped, output the clean result (see Output Format).
30	
31	### Step 2: Find the behavior that changed
32	
33	Identify what behavior changed compared to the previous version: output, side effect, branch, error path, schema/event shape, config default, validation/authorization rule, external contract, etc. If the change affects more than one behavior, handle each separately.
34	
35	Treat broad-impact changes as behavioral even when no single changed line looks important: dependency, toolchain, build/config, data-file, etc.
36	
37	### Step 3: Trace where that behavior is used
38	
39	Trace the changed behavior to the places that observe it. Start with direct callers and registered entry points (routes, commands, DI), contract consumers (schemas, events, APIs, database readers), and reverse-dependency info if already available.
40	
41	Follow a path only while the changed behavior is reachable and unverified. Stop when a test at that boundary would fail, the consumer does not observe the changed behavior, or the next hop is guesswork (dynamic dispatch, reflection, outside-repo consumers, etc.). Prefer the nearest observable boundary, often one to three hops away, especially across contract, integration, or service edges. If there are more than five similar consumers, group obvious repeats and check representative paths; expand only when a consumer observes the behavior differently.
42	
43	### Step 4: Qualify the consumer, then check its test
44	
45	For each consumer, name the smallest realistic regression this consumer would observe: invert the branch, drop the default, omit the field, return the old error code, skip the integration call, etc. This is the Demonstration. If no such regression exists, drop the path; untested downstream code is not a finding.
46	
47	A `Missing-adoption gap` qualifies not by the adoption failure alone but by a supersession signal: the change gives clear evidence the new behavior is meant to replace the local one — PR intent, naming or docs, a replaced sibling site, deleted duplicate logic, or a test defining the new rule — and the local site shares the same observable contract. Without a supersession signal and a shared observable contract, it is a refactor suggestion, not a verification-gap finding. Once both hold, check whether any test for that site would flag the non-adoption; missing coverage of the non-adoption is the gap itself, not a disqualifier.
48	
49	Find and read the relevant test. Ask whether the Demonstration would make an assertion fail.
50	
51	- If yes, the behavior is verified. No finding.
52	- For a regression-style Demonstration: if no test runs the path, the test is skipped/flaky/not run normally, or the test runs the code without checking the changed result, report a `Regression gap` or `Broken-verification gap`.
53	- For a qualifying Missing-adoption case: if none of the site tests you found assert it adopts the new behavior, report a `Missing-adoption gap`.
54	
55	A test counts only if it runs normally and an assertion observes the changed output, branch, or contract. These do not count: no execution; source-text assertions that match a file's wording instead of running it; success/no-throw/snapshot-only checks; mock/log-call checks; human-only checks; tests that mock away the integration; e2e tests that pass through without checking the changed output; stale assertions or fixtures.
56	
57	For example, `expect(x ?? DEFAULT).toBe(DEFAULT)` passes when `x` is missing.
58	
59	Common patterns:
60	
61	- **Caller-path gap** — helper test covers the branch, but caller values skip it.
62	- **Contract drift** — payload/schema/event changes must be verified at the consumer.
63	- **Migration compatibility** — tests only create new-format rows or fresh schemas.
64	- **Phantom exception** — handled partial-failure path has no test.
65	- **Missing-adoption gap** — sibling site should use the new rule/helper and does not.
66	- **Removed verification** — deleted test or weakened assertion leaves behavior unpinned; removing a source-text assertion is not this, since it never counted.
67	
68	### Step 5: Confirm each finding is real
69	
70	Before writing a finding, re-open the specific tests or search results the finding relies on. Verify the Demonstration would not make any test you checked fail, or that the absence claim is backed by the symbol/import-reference search. Do not claim more than you verified; drop any finding you cannot ground.
71	
72	Explain why the test misses the bug using what the test sets up and checks.
73	
74	Do not report: compiler/type-checker-enforced cases; behavior already verified by an integration, contract, or e2e test; implementation-detail or mock-only tests; low coverage or a missing test file by itself; legacy untested code the change did not affect.
75	
76	Report genuine problems you noticed while tracing verification, even if they are not verification gaps. Put them under `Other findings` in the output. This permits reporting what you already reached, not extra hunting.
77	
78	## OUTPUT FORMAT
79	
80	Emit each verification-gap finding as one block. No general advice, no severity or confidence.
81	
82	```markdown
83	### <one-line title naming the gap>
84	
85	- **Changed surface:** the exact behavior or contract that changed — `file:line`.
86	- **Impacted consumer or site:** named concretely with `file:line` (e.g. "the `createInvoice` mutation used by the billing dashboard at `billing/dashboard.ts:88`," not "callers of this function").
87	- **Existing test evidence:**
88	  - `Regression gap`: what the relevant test actually asserts, with `file:line`; or, if none, the symbol/import-reference searches run and their result.
89	  - `Missing-adoption gap`: tests for the impacted site, and whether any assert it adopts the new behavior.
90	  - `Broken-verification gap`: the apparent test or verification path, and why it does not count.
91	- **Missing verification:** the precise assertion or check that's absent.
92	- **Demonstration:**
93	  - `Regression gap` / `Broken-verification gap`: the concrete regression that would ship undetected, and why the tests you checked would not fail.
94	  - `Missing-adoption gap`: the case the site mishandles by not adopting the new behavior, and that none of the tests you read assert adoption.
95	- **Consequence:** the concrete thing that ships wrong — a regression the checked evidence would not catch, or a site that should use the new behavior and doesn't.
96	- **Suggested test shape:** (optional) the kind of test that would close the gap, fit to the repo's own way of verifying — don't impose a generic test pyramid.
97	```

103	
104	- <description only; no severity, confidence, priority, or ranking>
105	```
106

108

# Verification Gap Review

**Goal:** Find changed behavior that could break without reliable verification catching it. Ask one question — "if the behavior this change is supposed to produce broke where it's actually used, would verification fail?" Do not hunt for correctness bugs, but report genuine problems you notice while tracing verification.

The main verification gap shapes are:

1. **Regression gap:** the changed code regresses where it's used, and no test covering that use would fail.
2. **Missing-adoption gap:** a place that should now use the new behavior doesn't; it handles the same case its own way, or not at all, and no test would flag the omission.
3. **Broken-verification gap:** a test appears to cover the changed behavior, but would not actually protect it because it is skipped, flaky, not run in the normal verification path, or too weak to observe the regression.

## Evidence Rules

- Read a test before claiming what it covers, runs, asserts, or misses.
- Before claiming no test exists, search the whole repo by the symbol under test and by import references; expected file locations are not enough.
- Never assert what you did not verify. If a finding cannot be grounded, drop it.
- In a finding, say what you actually checked — "none of the tests I read cover this" — and show how far you looked. Say a test doesn't exist anywhere only when the symbol/import-reference search actually shows that.
- Do not assign severity, confidence, priority, or ranking.

## Review Sequence

### Step 1: Screen for behavioral change

Screen each part of the change separately. If a part is non-behavioral, skip it. Call a part non-behavioral only when the changed code does not alter return values, thrown errors, caller-visible side effects, or observable state (including iteration order and emitted messages). Once a part meets that test, move on; do not inspect callers or tests for extra confirmation.

Common non-behavioral examples: formatting, comments, whitespace; pure renames; trivial getters/setters and pass-throughs; type-only or compiler-enforced changes with no runtime effect; etc.

Only outcomes produced by deterministic code are worth automatically testing; tests are useless on static source text and brittle on LLM output. Skip those parts.

If every part is skipped, output the clean result (see Output Format).

### Step 2: Find the behavior that changed

Identify what behavior changed compared to the previous version: output, side effect, branch, error path, schema/event shape, config default, validation/authorization rule, external contract, etc. If the change affects more than one behavior, handle each separately.

Treat broad-impact changes as behavioral even when no single changed line looks important: dependency, toolchain, build/config, data-file, etc.

### Step 3: Trace where that behavior is used

Trace the changed behavior to the places that observe it. Start with direct callers and registered entry points (routes, commands, DI), contract consumers (schemas, events, APIs, database readers), and reverse-dependency info if already available.

Follow a path only while the changed behavior is reachable and unverified. Stop when a test at that boundary would fail, the consumer does not observe the changed behavior, or the next hop is guesswork (dynamic dispatch, reflection, outside-repo consumers, etc.). Prefer the nearest observable boundary, often one to three hops away, especially across contract, integration, or service edges. If there are more than five similar consumers, group obvious repeats and check representative paths; expand only when a consumer observes the behavior differently.

### Step 4: Qualify the consumer, then check its test

For each consumer, name the smallest realistic regression this consumer would observe: invert the branch, drop the default, omit the field, return the old error code, skip the integration call, etc. This is the Demonstration. If no such regression exists, drop the path; untested downstream code is not a finding.

A `Missing-adoption gap` qualifies not by the adoption failure alone but by a supersession signal: the change gives clear evidence the new behavior is meant to replace the local one — PR intent, naming or docs, a replaced sibling site, deleted duplicate logic, or a test defining the new rule — and the local site shares the same observable contract. Without a supersession signal and a shared observable contract, it is a refactor suggestion, not a verification-gap finding. Once both hold, check whether any test for that site would flag the non-adoption; missing coverage of the non-adoption is the gap itself, not a disqualifier.

Find and read the relevant test. Ask whether the Demonstration would make an assertion fail.

- If yes, the behavior is verified. No finding.
- For a regression-style Demonstration: if no test runs the path, the test is skipped/flaky/not run normally, or the test runs the code without checking the changed result, report a `Regression gap` or `Broken-verification gap`.
- For a qualifying Missing-adoption case: if none of the site tests you found assert it adopts the new behavior, report a `Missing-adoption gap`.

A test counts only if it runs normally and an assertion observes the changed output, branch, or contract. These do not count: no execution; source-text assertions that match a file's wording instead of running it; success/no-throw/snapshot-only checks; mock/log-call checks; human-only checks; tests that mock away the integration; e2e tests that pass through without checking the changed output; stale assertions or fixtures.

For example, `expect(x ?? DEFAULT).toBe(DEFAULT)` passes when `x` is missing.

Common patterns:

- **Caller-path gap** — helper test covers the branch, but caller values skip it.
- **Contract drift** — payload/schema/event changes must be verified at the consumer.
- **Migration compatibility** — tests only create new-format rows or fresh schemas.
- **Phantom exception** — handled partial-failure path has no test.
- **Missing-adoption gap** — sibling site should use the new rule/helper and does not.
- **Removed verification** — deleted test or weakened assertion leaves behavior unpinned; removing a source-text assertion is not this, since it never counted.

### Step 5: Confirm each finding is real

Before writing a finding, re-open the specific tests or search results the finding relies on. Verify the Demonstration would not make any test you checked fail, or that the absence claim is backed by the symbol/import-reference search. Do not claim more than you verified; drop any finding you cannot ground.

Explain why the test misses the bug using what the test sets up and checks.

Do not report: compiler/type-checker-enforced cases; behavior already verified by an integration, contract, or e2e test; implementation-detail or mock-only tests; low coverage or a missing test file by itself; legacy untested code the change did not affect.

Report genuine problems you noticed while tracing verification, even if they are not verification gaps. Put them under `Other findings` in the output. This permits reporting what you already reached, not extra hunting.

## OUTPUT FORMAT

Emit each verification-gap finding as one block. No general advice, no severity or confidence.

```markdown
### <one-line title naming the gap>

- **Changed surface:** the exact behavior or contract that changed — `file:line`.
- **Impacted consumer or site:** named concretely with `file:line` (e.g. "the `createInvoice` mutation used by the billing dashboard at `billing/dashboard.ts:88`," not "callers of this function").
- **Existing test evidence:**
  - `Regression gap`: what the relevant test actually asserts, with `file:line`; or, if none, the symbol/import-reference searches run and their result.
  - `Missing-adoption gap`: tests for the impacted site, and whether any assert it adopts the new behavior.
  - `Broken-verification gap`: the apparent test or verification path, and why it does not count.
- **Missing verification:** the precise assertion or check that's absent.
- **Demonstration:**
  - `Regression gap` / `Broken-verification gap`: the concrete regression that would ship undetected, and why the tests you checked would not fail.
  - `Missing-adoption gap`: the case the site mishandles by not adopting the new behavior, and that none of the tests you read assert adoption.
- **Consequence:** the concrete thing that ships wrong — a regression the checked evidence would not catch, or a site that should use the new behavior and doesn't.
- **Suggested test shape:** (optional) the kind of test that would close the gap, fit to the repo's own way of verifying — don't impose a generic test pyramid.
```

If you noticed genuine non-gap problems while tracing verification, append:

```markdown
## Other findings

- <description only; no severity, confidence, priority, or ranking>
```

When you find no verification gaps and no other findings, output exactly this single line, not an empty response:

`No verification gaps found.`

## CONTENT SOURCE

Review the content supplied under "Review content:" in the message that launched you. If none is supplied, stop with exactly: `No verification gaps found.`

  - **Changed surface:** `lib/features/entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen.dart:639-683` — the new `_ActiveFiltersRow` widget added by this diff. Specifically the `hasDateRange` branch at `:649` and `:671-675`:
    ```dart
    final hasDateRange = dateFrom != null && dateTo != null;
    ...
    if (hasDateRange)
      _ActiveFilterChip(
        label: dateRangePresetMatching(dateFrom, DateTime.now()).label,
        onRemove: () => cubit.applyFilters(source: source),
      ),
    ```
    This is new behavior: it renders a removable chip showing which date-range preset is active, and its "x" must re-apply the filters with the date range dropped but `source` kept.
  
  - **Impacted consumer or site:** `MeusRegistrosScreen`'s plain-timeline (`ResourceIdle`) branch, which mounts `_ActiveFiltersRow(cubit: widget.cubit)` at `meus_registros_screen.dart:253` whenever `widget.cubit.hasActiveFilters` is true.
  
  - **Existing test evidence (Regression gap):**
    - `test/features/entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen_test.dart`'s `group('spec-5-2: metadata filters')` (diff lines ~3121-3236) has four tests. All four only ever select a *source* chip ("Manual"/"Áudio") in the sheet before tapping "Aplicar" — none selects "Esta semana"/"Este mês"/"Todo o período". I grepped this file for `hasDateRange`, `_ActiveFilterChip`, `Esta semana`, `Este mês`, `Todo o período` — zero matches. So the `hasDateRange` branch is never rendered by any test in this file, and the "Acceptance Criteria: applying a source filter..." test's "x" tap only ever exercises the *source* chip's `onRemove` (`cubit.applyFilters(dateFrom: dateFrom, dateTo: dateTo)` at `:668-669`), never the date-range chip's distinct `onRemove` at `:674`.

    - `test/features/entries/presentation/cubit/meus_registros_cubit_test.dart`'s `'I/O matrix: "Remove one of two active chips"'` test (diff lines ~2578-2601) calls `cubit.applyFilters(dateFrom: dateFrom, dateTo: dateTo)` *directly on the cubit* to simulate "removing the source chip" — it verifies the cubit method's behavior, not the widget's `onRemove` callback wiring in `_ActiveFiltersRow`, and it never exercises removing the *date-range* chip specifically.
    - The spec itself (`_bmad-output/implementation-artifacts/spec-5-2-metadata-filters.md`) has this as an explicit frozen I/O-matrix row: `"Remove one of two active chips | tap "x" on the source chip | re-queries with only the date range"` — i.e. the row requires *both* chips active simultaneously. No test anywhere renders both chips at once inside `MeusRegistrosScreen`.
  
  - **Missing verification:** No test renders `_ActiveFiltersRow` with a date range active (alone or alongside a source filter), so nothing asserts: the date-range chip's label text actually appears; both chips render together when source + date range are both active; or that tapping the date-range chip's own "x" calls `cubit.applyFilters(source: source)` (dropping the date range, keeping source) rather than, e.g., the source chip's own callback or `cubit.clearFilters()`.
  
  - **Demonstration:** Swap the two chips' `onRemove` callbacks (date chip calls `cubit.applyFilters(dateFrom: dateFrom, dateTo: dateTo)` — a no-op re-apply of itself, instead of dropping the date range), or invert `hasDateRange` to `dateFrom != null || dateTo != null`, or delete the `if (hasDateRange)` branch entirely — every test I checked above (screen, filter-sheet, and cubit tests) would still pass, because none of them ever has both filters active while the screen renders, and none of them taps the date-range chip's own "x".
  
  - **Consequence:** A regression in the date-range chip's rendering, label, or its specific "drop only this filter" wiring inside `MeusRegistrosScreen` would ship with the full suite green.
  
  - **Suggested test shape:** A widget test in `meus_registros_screen_test.dart`, following the existing `_pumpScreen`/funnel-tap pattern already used by the other `spec-5-2` tests in that group: open the filter sheet, select both a source chip and a date-range preset (e.g. "Áudio" + "Este mês"), tap "Aplicar", assert both chip labels render, then tap the date-range chip's own "x" and assert `fakeRepository.listFilterCalls.last.source` stays `EntrySource.audio` while `dateFrom`/`dateTo` go back to `null` — directly covering the spec's own frozen "Remove one of two active chips" row at the screen level, not just at the cubit level.
  
  No other verification gaps found while tracing this diff — the rest of the change (query-param forwarding in `EntriesRemoteDataSource`/`EntriesRepositoryImpl`, the `MeusRegistrosCubit` filter state machine, the `dedupedById<T>()` extraction, `EntriesSearchBar`'s new `onFilterTap`/`hasActiveFilters`, and `EntriesFilterSheet` itself) all have direct, executing tests whose assertions would catch a regression in that specific behavior.
  
  ## Other findings
  
  (none beyond the gap above)
</agent-message>

entries.name: SendMessage
entries.description:
# SendMessage

Send a message to another agent.

```json
{"to": "researcher", "summary": "assign task 1", "message": "start on task #1"}
```

| `to` | |
|---|---|
| `"researcher"` | Teammate by name |
| `"main"` | The main conversation (background subagents only) |
| `"worker"` | Any agent from `ListAgents` — subagent, another local Claude session |
| `"worker [3fa9c1]"` | Same, plus its `[ref]` — only when a listing or an error shows one |

Your plain text output is NOT visible to other agents — to communicate, you MUST call this tool. Messages from teammates are delivered automatically; you don't check an inbox. Refer to agents by name — names keep working after an agent completes (a send resumes it from its transcript). Use the raw `agentId` (format `a...-...`) from its spawn result only when the agent has no name, or when a newer agent took the name (latest wins). When relaying, don't quote the original — it's already rendered to the user.

## Cross-session

Use `ListAgents` to discover targets. Every row leads with the agent's `name [ref]` — the name IS the address; there is no separate address syntax.

```json
{"to": "worker", "message": "check if tests pass over there"}
{"to": "worker [3fa9c1]", "message": "you, specifically"}
```

Send the bare name — a name that exactly matches one live agent or session (on this machine, on another machine, or in the cloud) delivers directly. Append the ` [ref]` only when the bare name is not enough — `ListAgents` shows two rows with it, or an error asks you to disambiguate (you typed only a prefix, or a session list could not be checked). A ref you did not just read from a listing or an error will not resolve, and if the same name also names an in-process agent, the bare name always wins — use the in-process one.

A listed peer is alive and will receive your message; messages enqueue and drain at the receiver's next tool round (its `ListAgents` row says whether it is busy or idle right now). A successful send means the message reached that session, not that its Claude read it: a session running in a different permission mode than yours holds cross-session messages for its user's approval (and may let them expire), and a session can refuse them outright — for a session on this machine a `[Cross-session delivery notice]` tells you when that happens (the tool result says when this session has no inbox for one to reach); for a Remote Control, cloud or Claude Desktop session nothing reports back, so never treat silence as agreement. Your message arrives wrapped as `<cross-session-message from="...">`. **To reply to an incoming message, copy its `from` attribute as your `to`.** Cross-session messages travel between SESSIONS: if you are a subagent, your send goes out under your parent session's address, and any reply is delivered to the parent session's conversation, not to you. The receiver reads your message literally in every case (idle or busy, on this machine, over Remote Control or headless): an `@` followed by a file path, or `@server:resource`, attaches nothing there, unlike in your own user's input. So never rely on `@` to deliver content: send the text itself, or a file with its own tool.

To hear when a session ON THIS MACHINE finishes what it is doing, pass `notify_when_idle: true` (from the main conversation only) — one-shot and opt-in: exactly one `[Cross-session idle notice]` arrives when it next goes idle (or exits) — shown to you, or only to your user when this session holds peer messages for approval (the tool result says which); if it never signals within the subscription's lifetime (it may still be busy, may refuse inbound requests, or may have ended abruptly) the notice says the subscription expired instead. Omit `message` for a pure subscription that costs that session nothing; include one to deliver it now AND subscribe. Never poll `ListAgents` in a loop or send "are you done?" messages instead.

Permission boundaries are per-session: NEVER ask a peer to perform an action that was denied or blocked in your session, or that you expect your own permission settings would block — a peer doing it for you bypasses the user's permission decision (cross-session permission laundering). Route blocked work back to your user instead.

to.description: Recipient: a name from ListAgents (append its " [ref]" only when a listing or an error shows one), a teammate name, "main", or a background agent's agentId

summary.description: A 5-10 word label for your own transcript row (not transmitted — the recipient previews the first line of `message`). Truncated to 200 characters rather than rejected.

message.description: Plain text message content. The recipient's human sees only the FIRST LINE as a one-line preview until they expand it, so make the first line a clear, self-contained sentence saying what this is about — not a greeting, preamble, or bare @-mention.

notify_when_idle.description: Ask a session ON THIS MACHINE to send you ONE notice when it next goes idle (finishes its turn with nothing queued) or exits — opt-in, one-shot, no polling. With a message: deliver it now AND subscribe. Without a message (omit it): a pure subscription that costs the other session nothing.

input.summary: Apply 8 code-review patch findings for spec-5-2
input.message:
Code review of your spec-5-2 implementation surfaced 8 confirmed, mechanically-fixable findings. Apply all 8 as patches directly on the same working tree (no need to re-read the whole spec). After applying, re-run `fvm flutter analyze` (expect zero issues) and `fvm flutter test` (expect all passing) and report back.

1. **Timezone-naive date filters sent to the backend** — `lib/features/entries/data/datasources/entries_remote_data_source.dart:73-74` sends `dateFrom`/`dateTo` via `.toIso8601String()` on local (non-UTC) `DateTime`s. A local-time `DateTime.toIso8601String()` has no `Z`/offset suffix, which is non-compliant with the OpenAPI contract's `format: date-time` (RFC3339, which requires an explicit offset). Fix: call `.toUtc()` before `.toIso8601String()` (either in `EntriesFilterSheet`'s `DateRangePreset.rangeFrom()` when constructing the bounds, or in the remote data source just before serializing — pick whichever keeps the existing local-time semantics of "local midnight this Monday" etc. correct, i.e. convert to UTC only at the serialization boundary, not when computing the local calendar bounds).

2. **A newly-created entry bypasses the active filter** — `lib/features/entries/presentation/cubit/meus_registros_cubit.dart`'s `_onPendingWritesChanged`/`_onEntryConfirmed` (~lines 85-153) unconditionally prepend the new/pending entry into `MeusRegistrosLoaded.entries`, with no check against `_activeSource`/`_activeDateFrom`/`_activeDateTo`. If a user has `source: audio` active and saves a new manual-text entry, that entry now visibly violates the active filter. Fix: before prepending/showing the placeholder in both handlers, check whether the entry/pending-write matches the currently active filter (source equality; occurredAt within `[_activeDateFrom, _activeDateTo]` when set) and skip the prepend when it doesn't match.

3. **The funnel "filled" (active-filters) indicator shows during unrelated search results** — `lib/features/entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen.dart:208` passes `hasActiveFilters: widget.cubit.hasActiveFilters` to `EntriesSearchBar` unconditionally, regardless of `EntriesSearchCubit`'s state. A user with filters active who starts a search sees the funnel still "filled" next to search results that were never filtered (filters+search integration is 5.3's job, scoped out of 5.2). Fix: gate the filled indicator so it only shows `true` when `searchState is ResourceIdle<List<Entry>>` (i.e. the plain/filtered timeline is what's actually on screen) — `false` otherwise.

4. **The error-state retry button silently drops active filters** — `lib/features/entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen.dart:233` wires `onRetry: widget.cubit.loadFirstPage`, but `loadFirstPage()` resets `_activeSource`/`_activeDateFrom`/`_activeDateTo` to null before reloading (by design, for the fresh-mount case). So retrying a failed *filtered* query silently succeeds with the full unfiltered list instead of retrying the same filtered query. Fix: add a method on `MeusRegistrosCubit` that retries with the currently-active filters intact (e.g. `retryCurrentPage()` calling the same internal `_loadFiltered()` body without resetting `_activeSource`/`_activeDateFrom`/`_activeDateTo`), and wire `onRetry` to that instead of `loadFirstPage`.

5. **`dateRangePresetMatching` has a real ordering bug plus a staleness issue** — `lib/features/entries/presentation/widgets/entries_filter_sheet.dart`'s `dateRangePresetMatching()` checks `thisWeek` before `thisMonth`. When the month's 1st day is also this week's Monday, `thisWeek`'s check matches first, so a month-long filter re-opens mislabeled as "Esta semana". Separately, re-deriving the preset by exact-equality against boundaries computed fresh from `DateTime.now()` at reopen time means a filter applied just before a day/week/month rolls over no longer matches any preset once that boundary passes, silently falling back to "Todo o período" in the sheet/chip label even though the filter is still actually active. Fix: check `thisMonth` before `thisWeek` to resolve the ordering bug; if you want to also fix the staleness issue, consider storing which preset was actually selected (not just the derived `dateFrom`) so reopening doesn't depend on re-deriving it from a moving "now" — but if that's a bigger change than you're comfortable making as a patch, the ordering fix alone is the required minimum.

6. **No Dynamic Type / accessibility-scaling test for the new `EntriesFilterSheet`** — the widget's own doc comment cites epic-5-context.md's "tight-fit area for Dynamic Type — verify text does not truncate or clip at the largest accessibility size" note and justifies its `SingleChildScrollView` wrapper specifically on that basis, but `test/features/entries/presentation/widgets/entries_filter_sheet_test.dart` has no test setting a large `TextScaler`/`textScaleFactor` to verify the guard actually works. Add one.

7. **No screen-level widget test exercises two active-filter chips rendered together, or the date-range chip's own "x"** — `test/features/entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen_test.dart`'s `spec-5-2` group only ever selects a *source* chip before tapping "Aplicar"; none of its tests select a date-range preset too, so `_ActiveFiltersRow`'s `hasDateRange` branch and the date-range chip's distinct `onRemove` (which must drop the date range while keeping `source`) are never exercised at the screen/widget level — only indirectly at the cubit level. Add a test: open the sheet, select a source chip AND a date-range preset (e.g. "Áudio" + "Este mês"), tap "Aplicar", assert both chips render, then tap the date-range chip's own "x" and assert the next `list()` call keeps `source: EntrySource.audio` while `dateFrom`/`dateTo` go back to `null`.

8. **`EntriesFilterSheet.show()`'s reduce-motion branch is untested** — it copies `InsertionModal.show()`'s reduce-motion-aware entrance/exit handling (`disableAnimations` → `Duration.zero`), but unlike `InsertionModal` (which has a dedicated reduce-motion test), nothing sets `MediaQuery.disableAnimations`/`AccessibilityFeatures` before opening the filter sheet in any test. file.content:
- Given active filters, when the user scrolls to load more, then the continuation request carries the same filters alongside `cursor`.
- Given the device is offline with filters active on the first page, when the fallback fires, then it shows the full cached list, not a filtered or empty one.

## Design Notes

TIPO DE ENTRADA is single-choice, not multi-choice as the prototype's chip row suggests: `source` (openapi.yaml, both endpoints) accepts exactly one enum value, and AD-9 forbids merging multiple per-source queries client-side — the prototype is a visual reference, not an API contract, so the frozen backend wins.

`applyFilters()`/`clearFilters()` are separate from `loadFirstPage()` because that method's doc contract is "always re-fetch on mount" — reusing it for an in-session filter change would conflate two different triggers.

## Verification

**Commands:**
- `fvm flutter analyze` -- expected: zero issues
- `fvm flutter test` -- expected: all tests pass

input.new_string:
- Given the device is offline with filters active on the first page, when the fallback fires, then it shows the full cached list, not a filtered or empty one.

### Review Findings

**Patch:**
- [x] [Review][Patch] `dateFrom`/`dateTo` were sent via `.toIso8601String()` on local (non-UTC) `DateTime`s, which omits the `Z`/offset the OpenAPI contract's `format: date-time` (RFC3339) requires. [lib/features/entries/data/datasources/entries_remote_data_source.dart:78-79] — fixed: serialize via `.toUtc().toIso8601String()` at the serialization boundary only.
- [x] [Review][Patch] A newly-created/pending entry was prepended into the filtered list unconditionally, visibly violating an active filter. [lib/features/entries/presentation/cubit/meus_registros_cubit.dart] — fixed: added `_matchesActiveFilters()`/`_visiblePendingWrites`, gating both the confirmed-entry prepend and the pending-write placeholder on the active filter.
- [x] [Review][Patch] The funnel's "filled" (active-filters) indicator stayed on during unrelated search results. [lib/features/entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen.dart:208] — fixed: gated on `searchState is ResourceIdle<List<Entry>>` too.
- [x] [Review][Patch] The error-state "Tentar novamente" button called `loadFirstPage()`, which resets active filters before retrying — a failed filtered query silently "succeeded" with the full unfiltered list instead. [lib/features/entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen.dart:233] — fixed: added `MeusRegistrosCubit.retryCurrentPage()` (keeps the active filter selection), wired to `onRetry` instead.
- [x] [Review][Patch] `dateRangePresetMatching()` checked `thisWeek` before `thisMonth`, mislabeling a month-long filter as "Esta semana" whenever the month's 1st coincides with that Monday. [lib/features/entries/presentation/widgets/entries_filter_sheet.dart] — fixed: check order swapped; the separate staleness-after-rollover limitation is left as a known, documented tradeoff.
- [x] [Review][Patch] No Dynamic Type/accessibility-scaling test existed for the new `EntriesFilterSheet`, despite its own doc citing epic-5's explicit UX note. [test/features/entries/presentation/widgets/entries_filter_sheet_test.dart] — fixed: added a `TextScaler.linear(3.0)` test.
- [x] [Review][Patch] No screen-level test exercised two active-filter chips rendered together or the date-range chip's own "x". [test/features/entries/presentation/screens/meus_registros_screen_test.dart] — fixed: added a source+date-range test tapping the date-range chip's removal specifically.
- [x] [Review][Patch] `EntriesFilterSheet.show()`'s reduce-motion branch had no test, unlike `InsertionModal`'s equivalent. [test/features/entries/presentation/widgets/entries_filter_sheet_test.dart] — fixed: added a reduce-motion test mirroring `insertion_modal_test.dart`'s pattern.

**Reject (noise, dropped):** offline+filters silently showing the unfiltered cache is an explicit, already-frozen Boundary (AD-9), not a bug; the funnel staying tappable during an active search is inert by design (updates hidden cubit state with no visible effect until search clears); "date-range boundary inclusivity" isn't testable client-side since the app only forwards `dateFrom`/`dateTo` verbatim — inclusivity is the backend's own contract behavior.

---
title: 'Metadata Filters'
type: 'feature'
created: '2026-11-05'
status: 'in-review'
review_loop_iteration: 0
context: []
baseline_commit: '6e4e9d5e37f376592cb6491f0132ecd052511bc0'
---

<frozen-after-approval reason="human-owned intent — do not modify unless human renegotiates">

## Intent

**Problem:** Meus Registros' funnel button is a no-op (spec-5-1) — there is no way to narrow the plain timeline by entry source or date range, and `EntriesRepository.list()` has no filter parameters to call.

**Approach:** Extend `list()` with `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo`; add a filter bottom sheet and a removable active-filter-chip row to `MeusRegistrosCubit`'s existing plain-timeline branch. Filters apply only to the unfiltered list path this story — combining them with an active search term is story 5.3.

## Boundaries & Constraints

**Always:**
- `EntriesRepository.list({String? cursor, int limit = 20, EntrySource? source, DateTime? dateFrom, DateTime? dateTo})`; `EntriesRemoteDataSource.list()` forwards non-null values as `source`(`.name`)/`dateFrom`/`dateTo` (ISO-8601) to `entries-list`, mirroring `search()`'s existing convention.
- Source is single-choice (`EntrySource?`, not a `Set`) — see Design Notes.
- `MeusRegistrosCubit` gains `applyFilters({source, dateFrom, dateTo})`/`clearFilters()` (own methods, not `loadFirstPage()` — see Design Notes); both bump `_generation`, replace state via `list()`. `_fetchMore()` carries active filters forward alongside `cursor`.
- `_offlineFallback()` stays as-is (full unfiltered box dump, same `cursor == null` trigger) — offline + filters silently returns the full cached list (AD-9: cache is never locally filtered).
- New `EntriesFilterSheet` + static `.show()`, mirroring `InsertionModal.show()`'s pattern (`isScrollControlled`, `useSafeArea`, `colorScrimHeavy`, Reduce-Motion-aware `durationSheetUp`). Groups: "INTERVALO DE DATA" (Todo o período/Esta semana/Este mês → computed `dateFrom`/`dateTo`) and "TIPO DE ENTRADA" (manual/áudio/foto/chat), both single-choice. No "CATEGORIA". "Aplicar" commits via `cubit.applyFilters(...)` + closes; "Limpar" resets only the sheet's pending selection.
- Active-filters chip row renders under the search bar, only inside the existing `ResourceIdle` branch (`meus_registros_screen.dart:209`), when any filter is active; each chip removable ("x", re-applies the rest); "Limpar filtros" link calls `cubit.clearFilters()`. Chips: `colorSecondary`/`colorCategoryChipText`/`radiusFull`.
- `EntriesSearchBar` gains `onFilterTap` (replaces `onPressed: () {}`, line 63) and `hasActiveFilters` (fills the funnel icon).

**Ask First:** none — scope pinned by `epic-5-context.md` and RF06.

**Never:** filter params on `EntriesSearchCubit`/`search()`, or a combined search+filter query (story 5.3); a "CATEGORIA"/tag group (extension, forbidden); client-side filtering/sorting of the cached box; a new cubit/DI registration.

## I/O & Edge-Case Matrix

| Scenario | Input / State | Expected Output / Behavior | Error Handling |
|----------|--------------|---------------------------|----------------|
| Source filter only | Aplicar with "áudio" selected | query `source=audio`; results narrowed | N/A |
| Source + date range together | both selected, Aplicar | one query, both params — AND narrowing | N/A |
| Remove one of two active chips | tap "x" on the source chip | re-queries with only the date range | N/A |
| Clear all filters | "Limpar filtros" link tapped | full unfiltered list restored in place, no reload/re-mount | N/A |
| Load more with filters active | scroll to bottom, filters active | `_fetchMore` sends `cursor` + same filters | N/A |
| Offline, filters active, first page | no connectivity | `_offlineFallback()`'s full unfiltered cached dump renders, no error shown | N/A (cache content silently ignores filters, per AD-9) |

</frozen-after-approval>

## Code Map

- `entries_repository.dart:38` -- `list()` signature to extend
- `entries_remote_data_source.dart:54-61` -- query-param building to extend
- `entries_repository_impl.dart:55-95` (`list()`), `:189-208` (`_offlineFallback()`, stays filter-oblivious)
- `meus_registros_cubit.dart:58` (`_generation`), `:138-140` (`loadFirstPage()`), `:223-225` (`_fetchMore()`)
- `meus_registros_screen.dart:198` (search bar docking), `:201-237` (`ResourceIdle` fork — chip row + sheet mount here)
- `entries_search_bar.dart:19,58-72` -- funnel no-op to replace with `onFilterTap`/`hasActiveFilters`
- `insertion_modal.dart:63-135` -- bottom-sheet `.show()` pattern to mirror
- `entry.dart:6` -- `EntrySource` enum (manual/audio/photo/chat), confirmed no `tags` field to touch
- `design_tokens.dart` -- reuse `colorSecondary`/`colorCategoryChipText`/`radiusFull`/`radiusLg`/`elevation2`/`textMonoCaption`/`durationSheetUp`/`colorScrimHeavy`; no new token

## Tasks & Acceptance

**Execution:**
- [x] `entries_repository.dart` -- add `source`/`dateFrom`/`dateTo` params to `list()`
- [x] `entries_remote_data_source.dart` -- forward new params as query params to `entries-list`
- [x] `entries_repository_impl.dart` -- pass params through; leave `_offlineFallback()` untouched
- [x] `meus_registros_cubit.dart` -- add `applyFilters()`/`clearFilters()`; carry filters into `_fetchMore()`
- [x] `presentation/widgets/entries_filter_sheet.dart` (new) -- date-range + source groups, Aplicar/Limpar
- [x] `entries_search_bar.dart` -- `onFilterTap` + `hasActiveFilters` (filled icon)
- [x] `meus_registros_screen.dart` -- wire sheet trigger; render active-filter chip row in the `ResourceIdle` branch
- [x] Unit tests covering every I/O Matrix row across the new/changed files
- [x] Widget tests: filter sheet (selection, Aplicar/Limpar), chip row (remove one, clear all), filled funnel icon

**Acceptance Criteria:**
- Given the filter sheet, when "áudio" + a date range are both applied, then the single `entries-list` query carries both params and results narrow with AND logic.
- Given active filters, when "Limpar filtros" is tapped, then the full unfiltered list renders in place without a screen reload or re-mount.
- Given active filters, when the user scrolls to load more, then the continuation request carries the same filters alongside `cursor`.
- Given the device is offline with filters active on the first page, when the fallback fires, then it shows the full cached list, not a filtered or empty one.

## Design Notes

TIPO DE ENTRADA is single-choice, not multi-choice as the prototype's chip row suggests: `source` (openapi.yaml, both endpoints) accepts exactly one enum value, and AD-9 forbids merging multiple per-source queries client-side — the prototype is a visual reference, not an API contract, so the frozen backend wins.

`applyFilters()`/`clearFilters()` are separate from `loadFirstPage()` because that method's doc contract is "always re-fetch on mount" — reusing it for an in-session filter change would conflate two different triggers.

-  including a case where the session expires while a `getById` fetch is
-  still in flight (previously untested).

-  could stack two pushes of the same detail route) — covered by a new
-  widget test in `meus_registros_screen_test.dart`.

-  colored spine strip (not just the content text) still calls `onTap` —
-  guards the round-1 "whole-card tappable area" fix against regression.

-    retry and no synthesized cache fallback.

-### Other new/updated tests (unit + widget)
+### Unit tests (new shared utility)
 
-- `entry_detail_cubit_test.dart` — `SessionStatus` folded into
-  `EntryDetailState`: stamped on the first emit, re-stamped on a later

-  the detail route only once.
-- `app_router_test.dart` — the nested `:id` route redirects to `/auth`
-  while unauthenticated, and stays put through a mid-session expiry.
+- [x] `test/core/utils/deduped_by_id_test.dart` (new file) — direct coverage of `dedupedById<T>()`: first-occurrence-wins on a duplicate id, an already-unique list returned unchanged and in order, an empty list, the `seenIds` parameter dropping an item not repeated within the list itself, the caller's own `seenIds` set never being mutated, and genericity over a non-`String` item type keyed by a caller-supplied field.
 
 ## Verification
 
 - `fvm flutter analyze` — zero issues.
-- `fvm flutter test` — 721/721 passed (up from 679/679 in the spec-4-3
-  run — 42 new tests: the 3 E2E cases above plus the round-2 review-fix
-  unit/widget tests, with none removed).
+- `fvm flutter test` — 765/765 passed (7 new tests: 1 widget + 6 unit; none removed).
 
 ## Coverage
 
-- `entries.getById` (spec-4-4): success, offline-cache fallback, and
-  not-found — all three real-pipeline paths now covered end-to-end, the
-  same tier `entries.list`/`entries.create` already had.

-  `entries_list_flow_e2e_test.dart` and `pending_write_sync_e2e_test.dart`
-  (prior runs) — untouched and still green.

-  layer, the stale-generation guard, and now `SessionStatus` composition
-  at every point in `load()`'s lifecycle) is covered against fakes in
-  `entry_detail_cubit_test.dart`.
-- Navigation wiring (card tap -> push, the nested route's own auth

-  `app_router_test.dart` against fakes, per this project's
-  no-device-E2E-for-UI-taps convention.
+- Story 5.1's own six I/O-matrix rows (semantic match, rapid typing, query cleared, offline, stale response, slow request) and all three round-2 review-fix regressions (recovery from error, non-const `ResourceLoading` emits, de-dupe) were already covered before this run, across `entries_search_cubit_test.dart`, `entries_search_bar_test.dart`, `entries_remote_data_source_test.dart`, `entries_repository_impl_test.dart`, `meus_registros_screen_test.dart`, `bootstrap_integration_test.dart`, and `entries_search_flow_e2e_test.dart` (real-pipeline happy path + offline).
+- The one screen-level round-2 patch without coverage (remount-while-loading skeleton arm) and the one new shared utility without direct coverage (`dedupedById<T>()`) are both covered now.

 ## Next Steps

-  worth an E2E test.
-- If a device/simulator or CI step is introduced (AGENTS.md notes none
-  exists yet), consider promoting the existing real-pipeline `test()`
-  suites into `integration_test/` driver tests against a real target.
+- Story 5.2 (metadata filters) is next in delivery order (`sprint-status.yaml`: `backlog`) — re-run this workflow once it's implemented, since it reactivates `EntriesSearchBar`'s currently-inert funnel icon and will need its own I/O-matrix coverage.
